## 2. What to build

**§5 Replies, chains, Wrap up and tidying up** (prototype frame 5)
- **One action, Reply.** A reply posts at the bottom, in time order, visible to everyone, with one muted line quoting what it answers (click it to jump). No "Reply in thread", no second reply button. A reply to a reply joins the same chain.
- **A message with replies shows "4 replies · Alex, Mike ›"**; clicking opens the whole chain in the right panel as an item with a back arrow (root, replies in order, its own reply box, "Stop following").
- **Wrap up, by hand:** a "Wrap up" button in the chain's header and in the root's ⋯. It asks **"Which reply settled it?"** and offers **"Also mark as decision"** (ticked by default in a linked channel, CH53). The replies **leave the main stream** (a drawing rule: they stay rows for unread, search and export) and the root shows "✓ Wrapped up by Sofia: Jana 'Got them…' · 4 replies ›". Undo for 8 s; "Reopen" in the chain. **A new reply reopens it visibly** ("Reopened by Mike", CH54). Who may wrap up: the root's author, the channel's managers and admins; in a direct message, anyone in it who can post.
- **Reply chains** is a right-panel view: every open chain in this conversation, newest activity first, with "1 new"; wrapped ones below.
- **Tidy up afterwards:** **Reply to…** attaches a stray message to a chain; **Move to…** moves selected messages to another conversation (your own anywhere; others' only by managers and admins, and only to a same-or-narrower audience); when people in the target couldn't read the source, a warning first ("2 people who aren't in Founders will see this", CH55). A quiet event line in both conversations says who moved what; Undo for 8 s; nothing pings again. **Make a task** (§8); **Make a note** (Notes' call N19, recommended to Maciej: a note in your Notes Inbox quoting the messages with authors and times, titled with the conversation's name and date; Chat's ⋯ item and mode-row action land in CV-16 once N19 is decided and Notes' op exists); **Move to a task's comments** when Tasks accepts the proposal.
- **No automatic folding** in v2 (it can come back as a setting).

**§12 table rows**
| Action | Admin | Manager | Author | Member | Viewer | From |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Wrap up, reopen a chain | ✓ | ✓ | root's author | in a direct message: anyone in it who can post | — | CH30d |
| Reply to… / move own messages | ✓ | ✓ | own | own | — | CH30c, CH55 |
| Reply to… / move others' messages (same or narrower audience) | ✓ | ✓ | — | — | — | CH30c, CH55 |

**Edge cases this block handles** (§Edge cases)
- A reply to a reply → joins the root's chain, quotes the reply it answers; "N replies" counts it.
- Wrap up on a chain with unread replies → the replies leave the stream; the unread ones stay in Catch up as one chain item; search and export still find them.
- A new reply to a wrapped chain → "Reopened by Mike" on the root; the replies come back in place.
- Wrap up by someone who isn't the root's author, a manager or an admin → the button isn't offered; the op refuses.
- "Reply to…" on a message already in a chain → re-parents it; the old chain's count drops.

## 3. Acceptance criteria

**AC8 — Replies, decisions and tidying up**
- **AC8.1** Reply quotes and posts in the stream
- **AC8.2** "N replies ›" opens the chain on the right with its own box and Stop following
- **AC8.3** Wrap up asks which reply settled it, hides the replies, keeps unread ones in Catch up, undoes and reopens
- **AC8.4** Reply chains lists open chains newest first, wrapped below
- **AC8.5** Reply to… attaches a stray message
- **AC8.8** nothing folds automatically

**AC2 — A hackathon team's weekend (the hackathon cut)**
- **AC2.6** answers to a question sit in the stream with quotes, "4 replies ›" opens the chain, Wrap up closes it with the reply that settled it

**Tests that prove them** (file · name · AC · plain English)

- `supabase/tests/chat_chains.test.sql` · "chains, Wrap up, reopen, Reply to…" · proves AC8.1–8.5, AC2.6 · A reply to a reply joins the root; Wrap up needs a reply of that chain and the right caller; a new reply reopens; Reply to… re-parents and fixes counts.
- `tests/chat-replies.spec.ts` · "stream quotes, chain panel, Reply chains" · proves AC8.1, AC8.2, AC8.4, AC8.8 · Replies show a quote; "4 replies ›" opens the chain with its box and Stop following; the view lists open chains first; wrapped replies leave the stream and unread ones stay in Catch up.

## 4. Decisions that bind it

- **Shape** (round-3 §2.18, #23): one level. `parent_id` is the chain's root, `reply_to_id` what the reply quotes (the root or a reply of the same chain); a reply to a reply joins the root's chain. The root keeps `reply_count`, `last_reply_at`, `reply_user_ids` (for "Alex, Mike ›"), maintained by send, delete, move and Reply to….
- **Wrap up** is `wrapped_at`, `wrapped_by`, `settled_id` on the root (`settled_id` must be a reply of that chain). "The replies leave the main stream" is a **drawing rule** keyed on the root, not a data move: replies stay rows for unread, Catch up, search and export; unread ones a wrap-up hides stay in Catch up as one chain item. The stream's anchor must not move when it happens (spike 1's "Wrap up hiding replies mid-screen").
- **Reopen:** a new reply through `chat_op_send` (redefine it from its **live body**: it clears `wrapped_at` and stamps `reopened_at`/`reopened_by`: "Reopened by Mike") or `chat_op_reopen(root)`; the replies come back in place.
- **Ops** (round-3 §2.3): `chat_op_wrap_up(root, settled_id, mark_decision)` (include the third parameter, default false, so CV-14 doesn't change the signature: my reading), `chat_op_reopen(root)`, `chat_op_attach_to_chain(message, reply_to_id)` ("Reply to…": re-parents a stray message of the same conversation; old chain's count drops). Who: §12 rows above (root's author, managers, admins; in a direct message anyone in it who can post; viewers never). Activity rows `chat.wrap_up`, `chat.reopen` (#15). Index: `(channel_id, last_reply_at desc) where reply_count > 0 and deleted_at is null` for the Reply chains view; keep `(parent_id, created_at, id)`.
- **Client** (§5): the reply quote (one muted line, click jumps) and "4 replies · Alex, Mike ›" on the root; the chain as a right-panel **item** with a back arrow, its own box (⏎ replies, Esc goes back) and "Stop following" (`chat_op_follow_chain`, CV-5); the **Reply chains** view (CV-8b registered it; newest activity first with "1 new", wrapped ones below) and Details' section; Wrap up in the chain's header and the root's ⋯ asking "Which reply settled it?", the root line "✓ Wrapped up by Sofia: Jana 'Got them…' · 4 replies ›", Undo for 8 s, Reopen. Keys: `R` replies, ⏎ on a message with replies opens its chain (§16). Copy (#33): "Wrapped up by Sofia", "Reopened by Mike".
- Converted v1 replies carry `v1_thread_reply` and count as read with their root (CV-1).

## 7. Watch out

- `chat_op_send` is redefined by CV-2a, 5, 9, 10 and here: change only the reopen path.
- **Tier 2** (migrations, RLS, contracts, moduo-mcp, src/lib/runtime*): one `/code-review high` and one security scan of the diff at the end; scan findings go only into the hand-back.
- **Migration:** stamp provisional (re-cut on apply day, chat's order kept); redefine from live bodies (`pg_get_functiondef`); re-state grants by name (`DROP` + `CREATE` resets them); re-assert the Realtime publication if you publish a table; apply only on your migration turn, then `bun run db:test chat`; never `local:reset` or `migration up` (runbook, `docs/gotchas/supabase.md`).
- **Hot files:** `src/features/chat/store/*` and `src/lib/runtime.chat.web.ts`. Keep edits there small; another builder may change them too.
- **Public repo:** describe no security weakness in any file; tell the orchestrator in the hand-back.
